label: Disruption
definition: Modded clients used to disrupt, attack, grief, or cheat: crashing, griefing tools, aimbots/wallhacks/speedhacks, item or rank manipulation.

label: Asset Theft
definition: Avatar ripping, world ripping, model piracy, datamining, or content extraction from the platform.

label: Safety Evasion
definition: Mechanisms used to defeat platform-level safety controls: HWID spoofing, alt-account ban evasion, un-blockable clients, forced entry into private instances, VPN ban evasion.

label: Private Info Access
definition: Privacy violations against other users enabled by mods: IP grabbing, doxing, exposing hidden information (friend lists, blocked status), HWID logging, identity spoofing.

label: Mod Side-Effects
definition: Security risks to the user who installed the mod: malware, RATs, keyloggers, token stealers, account takeover via mod loaders, hardware damage.

label: AC Effective
definition: AC engine framed as good, effective, working, beneficial, justified, or necessary; defenses of AC against critics.

label: AC Ineffective
definition: Any negative sentiment, complaint, criticism, technical failure, or false-positive ban attributed to the AC engine.

label: Limited Platform Coverage
definition: Cross-platform inconsistency in AC enforcement (Quest vs. PC, Linux/Proton, mobile bypasses).

label: Performance Overhead
definition: Performance regression or technical failure attributed to AC: FPS drops, BSODs, launch failures, AV conflicts.

label: Loss of Useful Mods
definition: AC removes or restricts legitimate QoL or accessibility mods (FSR, face/eye tracking, OSC, captions, performance optimizers).

label: AC Privacy Concerns
definition: Privacy, surveillance, or kernel-access concerns about the AC software itself: rootkit/spyware framing, data collection, kernel-level access.

label: User Recommendations
definition: Concrete technical, architectural, or policy alternatives to client-side AC proposed by users.

label: AC Financial Motives
definition: AC decision attributed to corporate, investor, or business motives rather than user safety.
